limits: Source/document inspection only; possible harms are analytical risks, not proven defects. No implementation/interface or full R5 completion claimed. Perspective proposals clarify existing requested scope without unrelated demands.

perspectives.proposal: Prioritize one explicit usable conversion CLI/API contract with named inputs, outputs and repeatable commands before the miner measurements.
perspectives.user_problem: A useful next gain is completing an actual conversion workflow rather than adding another status checkbox.
perspectives.fact: S19 accepted finite R4 quality and R5 filters/calendar while R5-03 and04 remain open.

perspectives.proposal: State whether each S20 conversion is an operator CLI, developer diagnostic or product API, and claim only the interface actually delivered.
perspectives.user_problem: Diagnostic acceptance can be mistaken for a feature already available in the running application.
perspectives.fact: S19 quality work is a diagnostic CLI, not a new product button or server quality API.

perspectives.proposal: Freeze the finite selected pairs and observable conservation/loss/refusal criteria before implementation; leave other pairs explicitly out of scope.
perspectives.user_problem: A narrow serialization demo could be presented as closing all conversions.
perspectives.fact: Original R5-03 requires named pairs and supported constructs with conservation, loss, roundtrip and unsupported refusal; graph serialization alone is insufficient.

perspectives.proposal: Keep source identity and normalization choices visible; compare supported typed values/order/model semantics and report omitted information or refuse it.
perspectives.user_problem: Conversion may silently change ordering, omit metadata or discard behavior even when event counts match.
perspectives.fact: CSV mapping has optional timestamp/lifecycle columns and explicit source/timestamp ordering; BPMN uses a strict unsupported-construct gate.

perspectives.proposal: Retain empty traces/logs and unsupported inputs as named outcomes; do not turn refusal, missing measurements or failure into numeric zero or success.
perspectives.user_problem: Dropping empty or unsupported cases would make both roundtrip and benchmark results look deceptively clean.
perspectives.fact: S19 preserves undefined empty-trace precision, unsupported loop behavior and the original empty-log miner error.

perspectives.proposal: Use a small prospective measurement plan, bounded process/output/resources and reuse only justified unchanged dependencies; preserve the acceptance reserve and old evidence.
perspectives.user_problem: Repeated JVM/compiler runs can consume time and disk before independent acceptance.
perspectives.fact: S20 has8h with14:41:26Z native freeze,16:11:26Z deadline and new12GiB logical/allocated budget with free8GiB.

perspectives.proposal: Label exact algorithm/source/parameters/corpus and measured boundary; separate startup/end-to-end and algorithm timing if observed, and avoid cross-algorithm speedup claims.
perspectives.user_problem: A faster different algorithm or a timed wrapper can be misread as a SplitMiner speedup.
perspectives.fact: R5-04 names the real pinned upstream SplitMiner; the application also has differently named algorithms and quality witnesses.

perspectives.proposal: Name actual wall-clock/native measurement and memory metric/unit/sampling scope, preserve all trial outcomes and disclose warmup/repetition/environment limits.
perspectives.user_problem: An unlabeled memory number or overprecise time ratio may imply stronger evidence than the measurement supports.
perspectives.fact: A Java process has process-level memory and warmup effects; original criteria request separate time and memory comparisons.

perspectives.proposal: Keep interfaces and result explanations compact, target changed-path regressions and reuse independently justified unchanged witnesses without broadening S20.
perspectives.user_problem: Unrelated runtime rebuilding or broad old-corpus replay can delay useful closure.
perspectives.fact: S19 runtime0.7.5 and earlier accepted datasets are unchanged; remaining work is specifically conversions and miner measurements.
